[2023-03-14 23:23] led.lennon.atleticogranata : The U23 Structure is now available for who wants to give a chance to the younger players to train and to play some matches to prepare for the main team. Some rules for the U23 Team: 1) U23 teams play in a separate international league (see https://footballmanagerproject.com/Matches/Champ?champid=79) and a cup (https://footballmanagerproject.com/Matches/NationalCup?cupId=34) where all the U23 teams play together; 2) You will need level 7 academy to build a U23 structure. It costs 12M and it takes 20 days to be built; 3) Only <23yo players can play in the U23 team. Players that during the season become 24yo, will be moved automatically at the end of the season to the main team; 4) U23 teams have a minimal structure with some money from the sponsor and TV - really a small amount - to cover stadium costs and wages. The team cash at the end of the season is compensated with money from the main team, if below zero; 5) The u23 team takes the place of an existing BOT U23 team in that U23 league. All the players of the replaced team are simply removed and replaced with a set of useless u23 players with very low potential; 6) You can move players from the main team to the U23 team and viceversa but you need at least 3 days to do the way back (bureaucracy kills...) 7) The initial (default) players of your team cannot be sold, as every player that is put into your team when you don't have the minimum number of players from now on. They are unuseful and they can only be fired.  The team is fulfilled with unuseful player when a minimum number of players (2 GKs, 18PPs) is not reached. More details will come tomorrow, if I've forgot something.

[2023-08-08 21:39] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Some words about the new version of the ME (I'm open for comments in the <#1029510354792886392> channel): - A necessary malus is applied in the following conditions (when I specify for example DC=0, I mean number of players in the DC position =0):  1) if (DC=0 and DMC=0) => DC malus: 75%, MC zone malus: 25%;  else if (DC=0) => DC malus: 50%; 2) if (DMC+DC+OMC=0) => ML,MC,MR malus: 33%; 3) if (FC+OMC+OMR+OML=0) => FC,FL,FR malus: 50%; 4) if (FC=0) => FC malus=25%; 5) if (DL+DML+ML+OML=0) => DL,ML,FL malus=50%; else if (DL+DML+ML+OML=4) => DL,ML,FL malus=25%; 6) if (DR+DMR+MR+OMR=0) => DR,MR,FR malus=50%; else if (DR+DMR+MR+OMR=4) => DR,MR,FR  malus=25%; The malus value corresponds to the reduction of probabilities to win that the attacking or defending team (subject to the malus) has in the clash in that zone;
[2023-08-08 21:49] led.lennon.atleticogranata : - When the match is computed, the ME computes a coverage grid of the pitch, based on the position of the players. The grid covers the nine zones DL, DC, DR, ML, MC, MR, FL, FC, FR. When the action is in on a line (D: defensive or M:midfield), if the action is won by the attacker, until ME v22 the selection of the side (Left, Center or Right) for the next line was based only on the preferred side chosen by the manager in the lineup page plus some random. With MEv23, the selected side takes ALSO into account which is the side that is less occupied by the opposite team. This is much important when considering the effect of player ban or a substitution. The coverage matrix is infact computed each time the lineup of the team changes, and a hole in the lineup may bring a malus (see previous point) or just a low coverage that would push many actions of the opposite team in that direction;
[2023-08-08 21:52] led.lennon.atleticogranata : - When a clash is won easily in a zone, the attacker cumulates a bonus that is used to help the same team in the clash of the next zone;
[2023-08-08 22:00] led.lennon.atleticogranata : - An important factor of the clash is the energy of the players. The starting energy of a player is related to its form, while the energy consumption rate is related to the stamina. Having fresh players to replace from the bench the most tired ones is an important factor. Energy consumption is also related to the coverage matrix. A player that moves in zones where the coverage matrix of its team is much lower than the opposite time will get tired earlier.

[2023-08-29 05:50] led.lennon.atleticogranata : <:gbug:1045244930697740318> Something that can be considered like a bug has been removed, related to the recommended max price by the Advisory board. Now the multiplier is increased (up to 6) for fully trusted managers. Just some notes: - the multiplier goes from 1 (when the manager just registered) to a value greater than 2 (when the manager has trust 5.5) to a value that is about 6 when the manager is fully trusted (trust close to 6); - the multiplied number is half of the market price or the standard deviation  (whichever is bigger) of the market price for that players category. So if the market price is 16 and the market price std is 5, the maximum value allowed by the Advisory Board would be 16 + (16/2)*6 = 64 for a full trusted manager.

[2023-09-28 20:51] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Ok guys, I'm publishing changes for the red card conditional order bug and for young players bidding. An important change will be active by now about bids.  When you place a bid, if you didn't scout the player, your advisory board will evaluate the player on the basis of its actual skills and age and will provide a maximum price limit (it's more or less how it works now). If you have scouted the player, your advisory board will evaluate the player on the basis of the reported potential of the player (if more then one report, the weighted average potential will be considered).  To define the maximum price, the advisory board will multiply the base price (the average market price for that age and potential) of that player by a factor that is bigger the higher is the manager trust.

[2023-10-18 21:53] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Season 4 Update bug fixing complete.  I'm going to publish and fix even the last issue. To summarize: 1) A bug was affecting the promotion/relegation. Playoff/playout were formed correctly after the removal of abandoned teams, but I didn't take into account teams that resulted abandoned AFTER forming playoff-playout and before the end of the season. The bug then moved these teams to the end of the chart with 0 points even if these teams were assigned to a playoff/out. This had messed some championships, but I've tried to fix it as much as I could. To fix it, from season 4, teams are moved to the end of the chart only at the end of the championship, when playoff/out are formed. After that, they wait for removal at the end of the season but without being moved down. Unfortunately, I don't have another solution for this; 2) Some promoting/relegating teams didn't receive their season tickets money. I've found and corrected the bug, and I've also found a way to move the season ticket sell to the new season, so that every manager can see the amount in the cash page at the start of the season.  3) I've just executed a fixing procedure to return season tickets money to who didn't received.

[2023-11-05 23:05] led.lennon.atleticogranata : I've said that I wouldn't spend much time on it and I ended with the release of MEv29. This new engine will have the following main characteristics: 1) After I've checked that form has too big relevance on match result and after some investigation, I've reduced the form relevance. Before MEv29, a player with [Grade,Form]=[20,20] was equivalent to a player with [23.2,15], or a [20,15] was equal to a [17.4,20] (see first graph). With MEv29, the a [20,20] is equivalent to a [22.1,15] and a [20,15] is equivalent to a [18.3,20] (see second graph); 2) A new covariance matrix has been finally introduced. It's long time that the new matrix has been designed but the implementation has been really tricky. To summarize, there is more lateral influence for players, so DCs contribute more to the DL and DR zones and the same is for DL and DR players that contribute more to DC zone. The same is for all other lines. The heat map can be summarized as in the following graphs (the fist is for ME versions before 29, the second is for MEv29) 3) The last changes are related to GK. It seems that GK skills are not properly taken into account. This ME should solve the issue.   The ME will be published tomorrow late evening to be used for friendly matches and it will be available for official matches on Thursday.

[2023-12-03 10:15] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Before continuing to test yesterday's changes, I've checked if player drafting is working as it should.  Running draft routine for 60 weeks (5 seasons) and the same team, I've found that distribution of number of player works as it should (see https://footballmanagerproject.com/Community/Guide/Topic?id=7#chid5) and the amount of players drafted over a given level is as expected. [2023-12-03 22:53] led.lennon.atleticogranata : I didn't make it to publish, it will be done tomorrow with a more detailed description of changes. By the way, the update will contains following changes (that are still on DEV server): - Training under 100% before this update just boost the form and decreased the skill increment, that made very convenient to train <29yo players with low training to have their form always at the max. This is obviously not so acceptable. By next update, training at a percentage less than 100% will also, on the long run, damage the overall form of each player that it will take time to be recovered. For example, training once 50% will penalize the overall for of a quantity that will require 5 weeks to be recovered.  - Playing matches will make players form more constant and less oscillating. In general, each player will need to do some minutes on the pitch to have this benefit.  - There are some players in FMP that, due to a old bug (now removed), are still training and gaining skills overcoming much their potential. This "issue" has been removed, players with actual grade over their potential will see their GI go to almost 0 until they get 29yo. - The bug that prevent managers to bid more than 70k for a young and small rated player even if the player is scouted should have been removed.

[2024-01-06 14:58] led.lennon.atleticogranata : **Important Notice Regarding Player Trading in the Upcoming Season:** Starting from the next season, player prices for agents will be determined solely based on player ratings, and no longer on their potential. This adjustment is being implemented to address instances where some managers exploit the players value difference (between potential-based and rating based price) by continuously buying and selling the same player for substantial profits. This practice is obviously unacceptable, prompting the need for this change. Managers who have heavily invested in this strategy, accumulating a team with numerous low-rated/medium-potential players, can get anyway some profits selling these players after their development. We appreciate your understanding as we strive to maintain fairness and integrity in the player trading system. Thank you for your cooperation.

[2024-02-18 09:48] led.lennon.atleticogranata : An update related to form and rating visualization. Until now, values were approximated due to the fact that only the owner can see his team's players decimals while other team's players skills, rating and forms were truncated. In particular, until now, opposite team's form were heavily approximated (to /4, that it means that all values between 12 and 15.9 resulted to be 12 and all values between 16 and 19.9 were visualized as 16). This was motivated to make each manager to know own team's details and know less details about the other team's status. Averaging truncated values, moreover, was resulting in a average value that was underestimated respect to the real one.  To avoid confusion and conspiracy allegations, opposite team's form is now still truncated but to the closer integer (values from 13 to 13.9 are truncated to 13) and averages are computed taking into account that values are truncated (so 0.5 is added to each value to average) to minimize the error. For example, before the update you would have seen (Atletico Granata is owner)

[2024-02-19 22:16] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Inspired by a question from Mirel, I've made some changes for Academy Draft. By next update, there will be this blooming distribution vs draft age: In the horizontal axis there is the draft age, while in the vertical axis there is the blooming age. Gray line is the lower limit, player can't bloom before the draft (it's to make things easier for me from the programmer point of view). Blue line is the average blooming age for players while red line is the higher limit where 95% of the draft will take place. Only 5% of the players can bloom later than the red line (22yrs is the maximum age for blooming). This change will decrease dramatically the number of very late bloomers from now on. Lines -1sigma and +1sigma lines define the zone in which 68% of the drafts will take place. This is just a temporary arrangement, I will take into consideration other good proposals, if any (in <#1029510354792886392>, please)

[2024-06-07 06:19] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Development complete: ✅  limit age for very good players drafted by bot teams, to increase interest in scouting and scavenging through nations and leagues; I will provide some more details this evening, and I will publish also some info about this change in the FMP forum and in the manual.
[2024-06-07 20:56] led.lennon.atleticogranata : The details: Bot teams are now being monitored daily to ensure the completeness of their squads in terms of player numbers and types. The target number of players for each bot team is 30. If a team exceeds this number, weaker players are either released or placed on the transfer market. The most represented position (FP) on the team is typically used to determine which player will be released or transfer-listed.  When a bot team has fewer than 30 players, a new player is drafted, usually one that is already somewhat developed. Occasionally, even if there are 30 players on the team, to prevent the team from becoming too old, some players may be released (if they are too weak or old) or transfer-listed (if there is a surplus in a specific position). This reduces the total number of players below 30, prompting a new player to be drafted within the same day or the following days.  All these operations are performed randomly, with a low probability of occurrence, to prevent overloading the game database.  The simulated draft for bot teams uses an academy level that is lower than what is required for their category. For example, the academy level is set to 11 for first-tier teams, 10 for second-tier teams, and so on. Despite this, it is still possible for very good players to be drafted at these academy levels.  Starting today, when a bot team drafts a good player (with a rating higher than 3), instead of drafting a fully developed player, the player will be drafted younger. This change aims to prevent bot teams from becoming too strong and to make the players less noticeable to human managers, who will need to scout more diligently to identify potential new talents.  A simulation of 10,000 drafts with random potential ratings up to 6 shows the distribution in the graph. Consequently, there will now be a very small chance of drafting a player with a rating higher than 4. However, if unnoticed, these players will develop to reach their true potential over time.

[2024-06-26 21:58] led.lennon.atleticogranata : The new rules about Under bot team players.  - When a Under bot team is created, all players are assigned to this team by default, so they cannot be bought; - When an Under bot team is created in place of an abandoned under team, their "default assignment" status is not changed, so it can be bought if in the former abandoned team it was not a default player; - When a player is added to an under bot team because the team needs some players (total number of players in a team is below a given limit) the player is assigned by default, so it cannot be bought; - Sometimes, higher potential bot under team players are put into transferlist automatically and they obviously can be bought.
[2024-06-27 20:47] led.lennon.atleticogranata : New rule about Stamina, effective in MEv38 - Stamina will affect more (+25%)  energy drop during the match respect to now. As implemented actually (ME version <= 37), considering a standard coverage, there is a energy drop of 0.02 each action if player's stamina is maximum (25.5), this value can rise up to 0.0675 if stamina is minimum. With new ME, energy can drop up to 0.08 per action if stamina is minimum, while the drop for maximum stamina is the same as now. - Remember that coverage also affects energy loss. If a player is the only DC against 2 FCs from the opposite team, its commitment in the match would be greater and the energy drop could grow significantly

[2024-07-29 20:12] led.lennon.atleticogranata : As outcome of the FP confidence effect analysis, I've decided to modify it effect starting MEv39.  Until now, the FP confidence resulted in the modification of players' ratings as described in the first figure. Practically, a 10% loss in confidence for a player was equivalent to being moved one spot in the lineup (e.g., from FC to OMC, or from DC to DMC). By the next ME (v39), that will be published very likely on Wednesday, the effect of confidence will decrease (second figure), making less penalizing to lose some confidence in the main skill. This graph, with a comment, will be published in the manual for clarity.

[2024-11-09 09:26] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Few fixes added: ✅ Bids on players belonging to a team that enters the abandoned or the banned status are now automatically removed to prevent bids to block bidding teams cashes. A notification mail is also added to notify status changes and bids removals. ✅ Fixed a multiple creation of U18 team and modified the creation code to prevent another occurrence of the same issue; ✅ Modified the building update function to prevent the occurrence of the issue that blocked building completion last days  The promotion/relegation mechanism is almost complete, and it includes the following changes: - All leagues will have a minimum of two direct relegations (provided there is sufficient space in the lower tier) and one playout relegation to each lower-tier league. - All lowest-tier leagues will have a maximum of four direct promotions and one playoff promotion. Direct and playoff relegations will not be finalized (meaning that playoff matches will still be played) if the promoting team is a bot and the relegating team is human. - The highest group within a tier will have its promoting and relegating teams move to the lowest group of the next higher or lower tier (for example, teams from 3.1 will be promoted to 2.2 and relegated to 4.8, or to the highest available group). These mechanisms are designed to increase the movement of human teams to higher levels, creating more vacancies in lower tiers and enabling new teams to be added to the highest levels possible (by default, new human teams are added to the lowest human populated tier).

[2024-11-20 22:40] led.lennon.atleticogranata : The new promotion/relegation system is now live. Here are the key changes compared to the old system:  - The first groups of a tier are harder to win compared to the last groups. For this reason, teams relegated from higher leagues with a better position in the standings are relegated to the last groups of lower leagues. This general principle is applied when determining the relegation league for each chart position. - When a team is relegated from an upper league, it cannot be replaced by a bot team from the lower league, even if playoff/playout matches are played to completion. During the season update, the switch between a human team from the upper league and a bot team from the lower league simply does not take place. - If a human team loses the playoff final against a bot team, the human team is still promoted. However, this will not apply if the human team does not qualify for the final. - Bot teams can only be promoted to an upper league if they replace another bot team. - There will always be 2 direct relegations for each league (except in lower-tier leagues) and as many playout relegations across the tier as there are groups in the lower tier. For example, in Tier 2 (with 2 groups), if there is only one league in Tier 3, there will be 4 direct relegations (2 from each of 2.1 and 2.2) and 1 playout relegation from 2.2. - There will be a maximum of 4 direct promotions from the lower league. For example, in a system with 3 tiers and only one league at Tier 3, there will be 4 direct promotions and 1 playoff promotion from League 3.1. Of the direct promotions, 2 teams will go to 2.1 and 2 to 2.2, while the playoff promotion will be assigned to 2.2.  Additionally, there is another important change to consider: - Bot teams will gradually be adjusted to match the level they play in. For example, if a strong bot team is relegated, its stronger players will automatically be placed on the transfer list.

[2024-12-25 15:12] led.lennon.atleticogranata : ✅ A small update has been made to the process of selecting home and away teams in the Clubs' Ranking Cup groups. Previously, matches were arranged so that the best-ranked team always played at home and the worst-ranked team always played away, with a 30% chance of reversing the home/away assignment. This setup often resulted in one team playing all its Ranking Cup group matches at home. From now on, the home/away assignments have been adjusted to prevent this issue. Starting with the next Ranking Cup, the first and second-ranked teams in each group will have two home matches, while the third and fourth-ranked teams will have one home match.

[2025-01-04 09:06] led.lennon.atleticogranata : The update of the game libraries has been a challenging process. On January 2nd, I successfully removed critical security vulnerabilities by updating the software to the 3.1.x subrelease of the libraries. However, my main concern has been the outdated nature of these libraries, which date back to 2019. With the latest library version already at 9.0 and the closest stable release at 8.0 (2023) still lacking full support, I decided to attempt an intermediate upgrade to version 6.0 (2021). This upgrade presented significant compatibility issues, and after dedicating an entire day to troubleshooting (nearly giving up last night), I managed to get the DEV and TEST servers running. While progress has been made—resolving approximately 70% of the issues—some website pages are still not fully functional and require further work. It’s important to note that this update will not bring immediate visible improvements to the game itself. You might notice slightly faster response times on the site, but the real value lies in laying the groundwork for the game's future. By transitioning to newer technologies, we ensure the game's long-term stability and open up possibilities for advanced features to be integrated over time. Today, I will continue working to resolve the remaining issues, and I am optimistic about completing the process before the end of the day.

New Dialog Box Format for Stadium Seat Construction and Team Removal A new dialog box format has been introduced to alert managers in two situations: - When constructing new seating in the stadium, if the new number of seats is lower than the previous one, which implies a reduction in seats. - Removing one of their teams.  2. Tracking of Team Abandonment Starting this weekend, we have introduced tracking for cases where managers abandon one of their teams. From now on, abandoning a team will result in increasing waiting times depending on how many teams a manager has started and later abandoned: - 1 team: 31 days - 2 teams: 40 days - 3 teams: 60 days - 4 teams: 90 days - 5 teams: 150 days - 6 or more teams: 360 days  3. Automatic Website Monitoring and Crash Recovery To prevent further extended downtimes, we have introduced an automatic website monitoring system. This system will restore functionality in the event of a site crash and will provide continuous statistics about the system’s status. This is useful for providing site administrators with insights into potential resource allocation issues.  4. Upcoming Changes to Player Evaluation An important change regarding player evaluations is on the way. This will affect both the maximum possible offer for player purchases and the price paid to agents. This update will particularly impact older players, who are currently somewhat overvalued compared to actual market interest.  We hope these updates improve your experience and help you manage your teams even more effectively! Stay tuned for more improvements coming soon.
[2025-02-09 14:59] led.lennon.atleticogranata : I'm finalizing the changes to the Market computation system. A new page will be available where you can calculate values for any combination of age, rating, and potential. Keep in mind that these values are based on actual transfers and are updated each season.  Since the new pricing system results in significantly lower prices for older players (approximately half of the previous values), the transition will be implemented gradually over the course of an entire season. When the new prices are higher than the old ones, they will take effect immediately. However, when the new prices are lower, the adjustment will be phased in progressively.

[2025-03-23 22:13] led.lennon.atleticogranata : **Here's the new paragraph about Players' market, to be published soon with the game update.** The market is managed by an international association that monitors player prices and reports any off-market transactions. Each time a player is bought or sold, the market records the price, age, and quality of the player, and subsequently updates the average price for that category of players.  With the latest update, the spending limit has been removed for teams managed by coaches with an advisory board trust level higher than 5. The advisory board will continue to impose this limitation only for new managers, preventing them from making transactions that could harm their team's financial sustainability.  As stated at the end of season 9, the market value will regulate player transfers by setting a maximum transfer cap at a predefined multiple of the player's market value, which depends on their rating, age, and potential. This value is determined by the player's national federation but is applied uniformly across the entire FMP world.  As buyers, you will not have a spending limit. However, the economic revenue for the selling team will be limited by the federation's transfer cap. Any excess amount will go to the player's federation and will later be redistributed among teams in that federation as national cup prizes.  The selling team will be notified in all relevant contexts when listing a player for sale or accepting an offer.  At the beginning of season 10, this issue will mainly affect younger players (<23 years old) because the market has not yet fully learned how to evaluate them. Over time, this assessment will improve, and only in exceptional cases will the seller's revenue be capped. In such cases, the seller may prefer to keep the player until they develop further and the market properly recognizes their value.  A link next to the price limitation warning will direct managers to this section of the manual to explain how the new transfer caps work.

[2025-03-30 22:06] led.lennon.atleticogranata : **Market Evaluation System Update** The player market evaluation system has been improved, particularly for young players with high potential values. In previous seasons, many low-rated players with good potential were sold at low purchase prices, leading to an overall low average market valuation for such players.  To address this issue, the market now considers not only the player's current rating but also a projected rating that reflects their potential future value once they fully develop. This adjustment increases the player's market value, impacting both: - The maximum amount a team can receive when selling the player. - The value generated when the player is sold through an agent.  **Match Engine Adjustments** The Match Engine (ME) has undergone slight adjustments concerning goalkeeper skills, specifically Agility and Set Pieces. [2025-11-14 22:44] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Last days I was working on the new mechanism to help lower-level division teams to move to upper teams. I've finally completed the design and almost completely tested this new feature.  This is the new rule that will be applied for the next season:  **NEW RULE: Replacement of Bot Teams in Upper Leagues** - Whenever a league contains at least 3 bot teams, after applying all previous rules, and there are human-managed teams in lower leagues that finished 8th place or better, the best among these human teams (across all groups of the lower tier, ranked by points, goal difference, and goals scored) will be promoted in place of the worst bot team of the upper league. - If the upper league contains 5 bot teams, the two worst bot teams are relegated and replaced by the two best eligible human teams from the lower tier. If it contains 7 bot teams, the three worst bot teams are replaced, and so on (starting from 3, 1 replacement every 2 bot teams).

For this reason, the optional HERO Mode has been introduced. - HERO Mode can be activated only at the Manager level, not at the Team level. Being a HERO requires bravery. - When HERO Mode is active, the rules that protect human teams from relegation when a bot team would otherwise take their place do not apply. - Likewise, the rule that replaces the weakest bot teams in upper leagues with the best-performing human teams from lower leagues will not apply to managers playing in HERO Mode. - HERO Mode can be enabled or disabled at any time, without limitations. However, activating it will be publicly visible on the manager’s profile, together with a counter showing how many consecutive days the manager has bravely chosen to play in this mode. - The modality a manager is playing (HERO or not) is visible only in the manager page and the team page. [2025-11-27 07:06] led.lennon.atleticogranata : 📢 Ranking Cup Format Update Dear managers, the time has come to introduce some meaningful adjustments to our competitions. The Ranking Cup will undergo a slight format revision, and before finalizing the decision I would like to hear your opinion. The new Ranking Cup may include one or two additional matchday and may adopt one of the following formats:  🟥 Option 1 – Playoffs Within the Same Group Group Stage: 8 groups of 4 teams (same as now) New placement matches: • 1st vs 2nd of the same group → winner to 1–8 bracket, loser to 9–16 bracket • 3rd vs 4th of the same group → winner to 17–24 bracket, loser to 25–32 bracket Final rounds: Quarterfinals, Semifinals and Finals remain unchanged.  🟦 Option 2 – Cross-Group Playoffs Group Stage: 8 groups of 4 teams (same as now) Placement matches: • 1st of one group vs 2nd of another → winner to 1–8 bracket, loser to 9–16 bracket • 3rd of one group vs 4th of another → winner to 17–24 bracket, loser to 25–32 bracket Final rounds: Quarterfinals, Semifinals and Finals remain unchanged.  🟧 Option 3 – Round of 32 with Four Brackets (A, B, C, D) Group Stage: 8 groups of 4 teams (same as now) Round of 32: • 1st of one group vs 4th of another → winner to Bracket A (1–16), loser to Bracket C (17–32) • 2nd of one group vs 3rd of another → winner to Bracket B (1–16), loser to Bracket D (17–32) Access to final brackets: • A vs B → winners to 1–8 bracket, losers to 9–16 bracket • C vs D → winners to 17–24 bracket, losers to 25–32 bracket Final rounds: Quarterfinals, Semifinals and Finals remain unchanged.  🟩 Option 4 – Keep the current Ranking Cup format No structural changes. The competition remains as it is now.  🎯 Why this change? This season the competition features 1,920 teams across 60 levels, including over 1,700 human-managed teams. The Ranking Cup is designed to increase ranking mobility between confederations and offer more variety, more matches, and an overall more enjoyable experience.

[2025-12-13 16:37] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Unfortunately, I've had to interrupt the CCC development because thanks to the collaboration of some managers (many thanks to them!) I've discovered that a weakness in the agent sell was being exploited.  This is the announcement that will be published in a while:  **Notice Regarding Player Valuation Exploit** During recent internal checks and thanks to the collaboration of some managers, we identified a weakness in the way the agent sale value of players was calculated.  The agent sale value is based on the potential evaluation provided by scouts. By intentionally hiring scouts with very poor potential evaluation skills, it was possible in some cases to obtain heavily overestimated potential values. Although low-quality scouts were supposed to reduce the final sale value to compensate for inaccurate evaluations, in specific situations this reduction was not sufficient, resulting in unfairly inflated agent sale prices.  This issue has now been corrected. From now on, unless a player’s potential is evaluated by scouts with high potential assessment skills (and possibly more than one scout), the agent sale value will be strongly penalized. This prevents any disproportionate overvaluation.  Database Verification In the coming days, a database review will be performed to identify cases where this mechanic was deliberately and heavily exploited.  • Recent transfers obtained through this method will be reverted • Older cases will have the unfair profits removed  No managers will be banned, as this was not a deliberate bug exploit but rather a poorly balanced feature. However, considering: • the large number of low-quality players involved • the intentional hiring of poor scouts • and the likely loss of most or all generated profits  this is considered a sufficient corrective measure at this time.  The goal of this intervention is to ensure fair play and economic balance for all managers going forward.  Thank you for your understanding.

[2026-05-16 12:10] led.lennon.atleticogranata : 💰 Transfer Market Update – Early Bidding A new mechanic has been introduced for specific types of players: - free agents - players from bot / abandoned / banned teams  Description: The first team placing a valid bid becomes the early bidder and gains a special advantage. If the early bidder remains the highest bidder until the end: 👉 they will receive a discount on the final price.  Discount = the lower of: - 20% of the final auction price - 4,000,000 ⓕ  Examples: - Final price: 10,000,000 ⓕ Discount: 2,000,000 ⓕ → Paid: 8,000,000 ⓕ  - Final price: 30,000,000 ⓕ 20% = 6,000,000 ⓕ → capped at 4,000,000 ⓕ → Paid: 26,000,000 ⓕ  Important: - The advantage applies only if the early bidder is still the highest bidder at the end - If another team overbids, the advantage is temporarily lost - It can be regained by bidding again and becoming the top bidder  The UI will highlight early bidding advantages with visual indicators (color / tooltip).  Note: This mechanic does not apply to transfers between active manager-controlled teams. 2nd Note: This change will be introduced in the next few hours  Thanks for your patience and support 💪⚽ We’ll get through this rough patch and come back stronger.

[2026-06-02 14:51] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Dear Managers, the Continental Club Cup Board has completed an important rules update for international qualification slots. ⭐  From now on, the number of CCC places assigned to each nation will no longer be decided at the last moment, when the new Continental Club Cup season is created. Instead, the international nations ranking will be frozen in advance, giving every federation a clear target and every club a better view of the road ahead.  What changes? ⚽ The CCC slot allocation will be locked at the end of the Ranking Cup for Clubs, after the final matches of week 6. That frozen ranking will decide how many clubs each nation sends to - CCC Level 1 🏆 - CCC Level 2 ⭐ Once the freeze is created, it remains valid for the next Continental Club Cup creation. The battle for international prestige still happens during the season, but the gates to the next CCC campaign close when the Ranking Cup for Clubs is over.  Where can you see it? 👀 The nations CCC ranking page now has two views: - Frozen ranking: the official locked situation used for CCC qualification slots. 🔒(it will be populated at the end of this week) - Current ranking: the live ranking, still moving as clubs gain or lose international strength. 📈 Frozen rankings will also be stored season by season. This means you will be able to look back and see which ranking situation applied in each season.  League tables and history 📜 From this season onward, top-level national league tables will use the correct frozen ranking situation to show which league positions are worth CCC Level 1 and CCC Level 2 places.  This also applies when viewing past championship tables: if a frozen ranking exists for that season, the historical league table will show the CCC qualification zones for that season. If no freeze exists for an older season, no CCC qualification zones will be highlighted there.
[2026-06-02 14:51] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Why this matters 🔥 This makes CCC qualification clearer, fairer, and easier to follow. Managers will know earlier in the season how many international seats their nation has earned, and the end of the Ranking Cup for Clubs becomes an even bigger strategic checkpoint. Every point, every upset, every deep cup run can now shape the continental map before the final stretch of the season begins. 💪  Server upgrade completed 🛠️ The server update process has also been completed. [2026-06-14 15:16] led.lennon.atleticogranata : **🏆 The Cup Winners Cup is coming! 🏆**  Managers, a new road to international glory is opening from next season. ⚽✨  The Cup Winners Cup, or CWC, is a brand-new club competition inspired by the old-school magic of national cup winners. It gives domestic cup heroes another way to step onto the international stage, even if their league campaign was not enough for CCC qualification. A simulation of the CWC computed for season 15  **🌍 Why is the CWC intercontinental?** Unlike the CCC competitions, the CWC is intercontinental. The reason is simple: in some continents, there would not be enough national cup candidates to create a meaningful continental tournament. Instead of building small, uneven competitions, the CWC brings cup contenders from all over the world into one global battlefield. More variety. More unusual matchups. More chances for a proper cup story. ⚔️  **🏅 How teams qualify** At the start of the season, FMP looks at the national cups from the previous season. Each valid completed national cup can send one candidate toward the CWC path. The best candidate is chosen from that cup run, starting from the winner and then moving down through the best-performing teams if needed. If the cup winner is already qualified for CCC Level 1, the CWC spot does not disappear. It passes to the next best eligible team from that same national cup path.  The selection order follows cup performance, then the result of the last cup match played, using: - round reached; - goal difference in the last cup match; - goals scored in the last cup match; - a random tie-breaker. .
[2026-06-14 15:16] led.lennon.atleticogranata : **⚔️ The preliminary round** Some CWC teams will start in a preliminary round, played during the first week of the season. The draw is seeded by ranking: - best-ranked team vs lowest-ranked team; - second best-ranked team vs second lowest-ranked team; - and so on.  The preliminary round is a single match on neutral ground. Win, and you enter the CWC main stage. Lose, and your continental season may still continue elsewhere.  **🏟️ The main CWC stage** After the preliminary round, the CWC main stage is completed with: - teams directly qualified from national cup performance; - winners of the CWC preliminary round.  The main stage has 80 teams. Apart from the preliminary round, the competition structure is currently very similar to a CCC tournament. This means a familiar group stage and knockout stage format, adapted to the CWC field.  Future format changes may be considered later, but not before after Season 20. For now, the goal is to introduce the competition in a stable and familiar shape.  **🔁 What happens to teams eliminated in the CWC preliminary round?** This is important: losing the CWC preliminary round does not automatically end a club’s international hopes. Teams eliminated in the CWC preliminary round can still be selected for CCC Level 2, if their domestic league position is strong enough. So the priority order is: - CCC Level 1 → CWC main stage → CCC Level 2  This means: - CCC Level 1 keeps top priority; - CWC main stage teams are protected from also entering CCC2; - CWC preliminary losers can still be recovered into CCC2.  In short: a preliminary defeat hurts, but it is not always the end of the campaign. 🛡️  **📅 Availability** The Cup Winners Cup will be available from next season. National cups now matter more. Cup runs now echo louder. And somewhere out there, a club that nobody expects is about to become an intercontinental problem. 🏆🔥 .

[2026-08-14 06:57] led.lennon.atleticogranata : 🎺🎺 **Saved Lineups arrive in the Lineup room** ⚽ 🎺🎺 Managers, the Lineup page has received a new tactical toy: Saved Lineups. You can now keep a small archive of ready-to-use match plans directly above the pitch. The new toolbar lets you: Add a new saved lineup slot from the current editor setup. Save the current editor setup into the selected slot. Load a selected slot and immediately make it the lineup used for the next match. Rename saved slots, including BBCode formatting. Delete a saved slot when the tactic board gets too crowded. Reset the current editor lineup and regenerate it from scratch. Each saved slot stores not only the players on the pitch, but also the bench, Conditional Orders (CO), and Rule Orders (RO). When you load a saved lineup, all of those details are recalled and the loaded lineup is saved for match use right away. You do not need to press the main Save Lineup button after loading, unless you make further changes afterward. Use this carefully, especially the first few times. Loading an old saved setup can replace the lineup, CO and RO you were currently using. Before a key match, take a last look at the pitch and orders. The dugout appreciates calm managers. 😄 More details are available in the manual: Saved Lineups manual page   **Small-screen lineup work also improved **📱 The Conditional Orders table has been updated to remain usable on narrow smartphones in vertical orientation. The table and its buttons should now be visible more reliably when screen width is tight. The sidebar access buttons on these small screens have also been adjusted visually, so they no longer risk wrapping one of the buttons onto a new line.
[2026-08-14 06:57] led.lennon.atleticogranata : **Transparency for elevated player-data access** 🔍 Some elevated users, such as administrators, now have tools to inspect reserved player data when needed, including blooming, form-related information, and owner-view data. Because this is powerful information, a visible access log is being added to the player page for everyone. The log will show whether and when an administrator accessed those reserved details, including accesses to players belonging to administrator-owned teams. This feature is intended only for support cases: for example, to investigate a player-growth doubt, form-behavior question, or similar motivated request from a manager asking for assistance. It is not a scouting shortcut, not a secret weapon, and not something to be used casually. 🛡️  Have fun with your tactics, guys!
[2026-08-21 15:20] led.lennon.atleticogranata : **⚙️ A little update about... updates**  After the many updates released during the first weeks of this season, things may look a bit quieter this week — and probably for the next weeks too. 🙂  This is my holiday period but, it doesn't mean development has slowed down. Actually, quite the opposite. I'm currently spending most of my FMP development time working on the Match Engine. And this time we're not talking about another adjustment or improvement to the existing ME: the goal is a new generation of the Match Engine. ⚽🔧  I don't want to reveal too much about it yet. This is already the second version I've built and then partially dismantled because I wasn't completely satisfied with the result. 😅  For this reason, I'd rather avoid announcing features or promising how things will work until I'm confident that the new approach is good enough. I'd rather show you something later than create expectations now and disappoint you afterwards.  What I can say is what I'm trying to achieve. The final goal is to make the ME more consistent with what is actually happening on the pitch: players should become involved in actions according to where they really are, rather than simply because their predefined position makes them eligible to participate.  At the same time, I'm building the foundations for something I've wanted for FMP for a long time: a Match Engine where the movement of the ball and the players can eventually be represented on a 2D pitch. 🏟️⚽ There is still a lot of work between here and there, and that's exactly why I don't want to give dates or make promises yet. But this is where most of my development time is going at the moment.  So, if the changelog looks unusually quiet for a while... now you know why. 👨‍💻

[2025-01-03 08:49] mirelodas : <:FMPStar5:1023847050305077289> ***GAME UPDATES*** <:FMPStar5:1023847050305077289>  <:FMPVote1:1287713536570556481> The new promotion/relegation system is now live. - The first groups of a tier are harder to win compared to the last groups. For this reason, teams relegated from higher leagues with a better position in the standings are relegated to the last groups of lower leagues. This general principle is applied when determining the relegation league for each chart position. - When a team is relegated from an upper league, it cannot be replaced by a bot team from the lower league, even if playoff/playout matches are played to completion. During the season update, the switch between a human team from the upper league and a bot team from the lower league simply does not take place. - If a human team loses the playoff final against a bot team, the human team is still promoted. However, this will not apply if the human team does not qualify for the final. - Bot teams can only be promoted to an upper league if they replace another bot team. - There will always be 2 direct relegations for each league (except in lower-tier leagues) and as many playout relegations across the tier as there are groups in the lower tier. For example, in Tier 2 (with 2 groups), if there is only one league in Tier 3, there will be 4 direct relegations (2 from each of 2.1 and 2.2) and 1 playout relegation from 2.2. - There will be a maximum of 4 direct promotions from the lower league. For example, in a system with 3 tiers and only one league at Tier 3, there will be 4 direct promotions and 1 playoff promotion from League 3.1. Of the direct promotions, 2 teams will go to 2.1 and 2 to 2.2, while the playoff promotion will be assigned to 2.2. <:FMPVote1:1287713536570556481> Verified NT rule for the selection of the third qualified NT will be applied correctly during next season update

[2022-08-03 06:10] led.lennon.atleticogranata : About the possession, I've found the error. The number was reporting the percentage of the failed actions respect to the total of the failed actions instead of the percentage of the succeeded actions. In the case of the first match (see the detailed stats), the percentage would be 43/16 = 72% vs 28%. Even so, the stats wouldn't be so accurate, because from the point of view of the possession, the count should contains also the failed actions. I will do more to make the stats more meaningful. About the 1DC, the thing is still under investigation, but for sure in the "action battles", the only DC fighting against two FC allows the FC to win the actions almost always because the influence of the DL/DR is much lower in the middle of the box. When a battle in the box is won easily, the bonus that the attacker gains is so high that the GK can't do much against it.

[2022-09-21 16:19] led.lennon.atleticogranata : At this time, the current randomization is made, during draft: - Starting from potential, the final skills will be reached in 4 phases: Draft, pre-blooming, Blooming and post-blooming (pretty much as in TM) - A part (I call it PBB) of this potential is assigned to the Pre-blooming and blooming phase (62% [std15%] of the total development), then split again to be part in the pre blooming (60% [std15%] of PBB) and the rest in the blooming phase.  - The remaining part of the potential, once removed PBB, is assigned to the draft (60% [std10%]) and the rest to the post-blooming development.  *Note: 62% [std15%] means 62% in average, with a standard deviation of 15%.* Differently from TM, players can be draft with age from 14 to 17.99 (very rare to have 14yo players, though), but this doesn't affect the development of the player at the end of the bloom.

[2022-11-03 00:10] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Update done.  I'm working now to check better the probability function that creates the players. From what <@442730766200209408> said, the spread of the probability is too high. At this moment, the average level of draft for level 14 of Academy (the advised level for a top A team) is about 12.5/25, that is more or less 3.1*, with a sigma that is 2/25 (0.5 stars) for each draft. A sigma indicates the value you should expect for the 68% of the population. Then, if a new team is created with 30 players, about 20 players (68%) should have a final rating included in the range 2.6stars to 3.6stars, 8 players should be between 2.1 stars and 2.6 and between 3.6 and 4.2 and 1-2 players can be higher than 4.2 or below than 2.1. To avoid the creation of superplayers during the mass creation of new teams, I will remove the queues of the probability curves to avoid limit cases. Today (Thursday) I will work on this to implement it and test it with a creation of a couple of nations.

[2022-11-30 22:10] led.lennon.atleticogranata : I've found the numbers. The ranking points are so assigned: - Ranking match, 300 pts; - National Cup matches: 250 pts; - Play-Off/Out matches: 200pts; - National Championship matches: 150 pts; Ranking points are the maximum quantity of points assigned for each match. For example, when two teams with the same ranking points play in a match, 50% of the points are added to the winner and removed from the loser. When two teams with (for example) 1000 ranking points difference play in a match, the assigned points will be +40%/-60% for the best ranked (if wins/loses) and +60%/-40% for the lower ranked (if wins/loses), with difference 2000 points the percentage goes 32%-68%, 3000 points 25%-75% and so on.  Please <@442730766200209408> when the beers effect will finish (🍻 , maybe tomorrow) remember to add as weekly task the addition of the ranking points gain/loss to the match preview and to the match outcome

[2023-04-04 10:59] frejos : Guys which tactic do you think is best? i am tryin every match somethin else and no happy with it
[2023-04-04 11:01] mirelodas : When in doubt which formation to use, go with plain 442...it works for bots most of the time 😀
[2023-04-04 14:27] .jferreira : It depends your strategy and how you want the transition def-atk to be. You can have more DM to lure opponent players to your defense and use long balls to put the ball on offensive players without much confrontation(but idk how ME leads with player positions on offensive instance in general, so idk if this appoach is really good). The usage of M or OM is more about the covered area on confrontations and the chance to finish; if you use ML-MC-MR, they will generally pass or cross; if you use OML-OMC-OMR they will finish more times. If you want your FC to finish and others players just to feed FC, you can use bot formation, but you need to pay attention if one of your attackers is losing the chances more than normal, because he may be spoiling your attack
[2023-04-04 14:35] .jferreira : One example of long ball tactic, the idea is try to confront more on 2/4(not just on 1/4 because is more dangerous to start confrontations on there). But idk if this tactic is really good because is hard to test without defenders with good passing.
[2023-04-04 14:42] .jferreira : One example of short passing tactic, if you want to put training of Orc and Ply on players
[2023-04-04 14:51] .jferreira : One example of though pass, with variation where you use the DMC as a third MC. The idea is to use MCs to make confrontations more early and feed offensive players for them to finish, generally they tackle a defensive player trying to make transition def-atk, so is more likely the opposition team to have 1 less player defending
[2023-04-04 15:01] .jferreira : Wing attack example, is a tactic that is made more to provide a good support on transition def-atk, DMC instead MC tends to be fundamental because DL-R may leave their position and you need a player that may cover at least a little side defensive area. You use ML-R instead OML-R because you need more support on transitions and because you don't want they to finish, you prepare they to be efficient on dribbling and crossing.

[2023-07-28 06:07] led.lennon.atleticogranata : There are two points. The first is that if I describe the idea behind the ME, the national sport becomes focusing on how the idea could be made better (no matter how the implementation effort could be) and what it doesn't work, so I should spend most of my time in explaining what is the reason of each detail. The ME idea is the outcome of a compromise between Pinco Pallini's idea (that I found great) and mine implementation, fully described in a TM Conference. I have to find the time to better describe it. The second point is that one of the aim of the Match Viewer is to better show how each clash is computed and why sometimes there are some strange results. I fully understand that too often the match results don't satisfy many managers (I'm one of these) and that the engine can be improved. The introduction of the Match Viewer will be useful also for this reason, it will help me to understand if the randomness level is adequate to what it should be and if something needs to be changed.

[2023-08-01 13:25] luchocogo : For starter team, try to fit the best tactic according to the players you have. As others mentioned, we dont know much about the ME. So use friendlies to try different tactics.  About the second question, it depends on your long term strategy. You can buy old players (Its important that they have a lot of experience, like 35+), and try to get good results on league/cup. If you accomplish that, the money prizes would make it worth. On the other hand, if you fail to get top positions, that will result in less money, and maybe will be difficult to keep a competitive team when your older players start retiring. If you don't want to take the risk, probably is better to build a young squad, and focus on increase structures, so in a couple of season you will have a good team and good finances with less risks.  Ofc you can mix both strategies.

[2023-09-22 14:37] .jferreira : Slowing the text is not the matter, the problem is how text is presented inside an "action storyline", how you organized the main actions and the transitions. For example, you try to group actions using the start area and the main action, if you separate the transition actions and main actions, you can make a good resumed version with only main actions or you can make at least a good resume of transition actions.  One example: "Ball to Fortaleza which sets the action at the left of their defense. Aydın sets the action on the left side of the defense, tackled by Coppens. Aydın overcomes Coppens despite the strong pressing of the opponent. Fortaleza attacks on the left side. Luque looks for an opening on the left, trying to avoid the pressing from Padilla. Luque overcomes Padilla despite the strong opposition. Here comes Fortaleza on the left of its attack. Aydın advances on the left wing trying to cross, Padilla tries to stop him. Aydın overcomes Padilla despite the strong pressing of the opponent. A great action from Zafarin who overcomes easily Ferreira da Silva and prepares to shoot. Zafarin aims at the goal, but Dantas saves the score."  Could becomes  [transition tagged] "Fortaleza with the ball on DL(you can use symbol), Aydin(ever using color and you don't need to say what is the team) try to advance by DL and overcomes Coppens, {seems to have some lost actions}, (Luque is tryting to avoid the marking player, I'm jerk, can't understand?)."  [main action tagged] "Aydin try to advance by FL, overcomes Padilla and try a cross. Zafarin receives the ball and overcomes Ferreira da Silva, prepares to shoot and... Great save by Dantas!"  But this is not even the hint, because is necessary to qualify what are the transition actions(passing and dribbling generally) and what are the main actions(crossing, though pass, finishing, heading, long shoot...). The hint is making the mapping chart of the match, without this it will not work.
[2023-09-22 15:18] .jferreira : The report have also a lot of reference problems to actions, because it not says direct what is a dribbling, what is a pass, sometimes how a player gets the ball... It don't seems to follow a action flow.  The match actions needs to follow a flow that can be grouped by transition and decision(what I'm calling main action).  Transition is when a team have the ball and wants to put the ball on a better position to make a decisive action, if the actual position is not good to make the desired decisive action or if the marking on actual area have too much marking to surpass.   Decision is when a team wants to call some finishing action, it's generally an assist try, attacking action, kick and rebound, and sometimes don't have the assist try like on long shoots. Any position on the field can be used to make a decision action, on some field status you have bonuses even if the decision is a long pass on defensive line.  Field Status is also another important concept, mainly because FMP is a game based on statistical chance of something happening. Field Status would qualify how the transition is made in terms of how players cover the field, if you a player cover less the defensive line to cover midfield, the same for attacking players, if the team play more positional and with direct passes, etc.  For example, if a team make a tactical decision to be more offensive, when this team have the ball, the players cover more the midfield and attacking lines, and if the other team gets the ball, they can make a fast transition and take some advantages on poor defensive covering, these advantages making the players needing to make less confrontations on transition to attack while the field status is recovering to something more defensive(what also would demand some energy).  Well, I'll stop here, is kinda useless try to explain this just by text, because is not something doable without the mapping chart, and mapping chart is not a non-gay thing to do without the code.

[2023-09-28 20:58] led.lennon.atleticogranata : An important change will be active by now about bids.  When you place a bid, if you didn't scout the player, your advisory board will evaluate the player on the basis of its actual skills and age and will provide a maximum price limit (it's more or less how it works now). If you have scouted the player, your advisory board will evaluate the player on the basis of the reported potential of the player (if more then one report, the weighted average potential will be considered).  To define the maximum price, the advisory board will multiply the base price (the average market price for that age and potential) of that player by a factor that is bigger the higher is the manager trust.
[2023-09-28 20:59] led.lennon.atleticogranata : More details and explanations on this in a news and in a manual paragraph.

[2023-12-05 07:19] led.lennon.atleticogranata : You have a week to see its effect because this week training, because of an error, has been run on last Sunday, as I've announced somewhere else. So next training will run on Wednesday 13th.  About the use of training with percentage 50%-90%, if you train your player (for example) with 90% you will get a small form boost (+1.2/25) for the first week but also a even smaller long-term form penalization (-0.2/25), so, the first week the balance is the same as before (+1/25 for each 10% training reduction). If you restore the 100% training the week after, the long-term form penalization is restored (+0.2/25) and you'll see no changes respect to now. If you leave the training as 90% for more weeks or you try to boost the form even more, it will take time to restore the long term training.  See the examples in the picture, This is intended to prevent managers' use of 50% training as permanent boost for form, that is a non-sense.

[2023-12-08 23:31] .jferreira : maybe it's something related to reason why bid stay on "your bids" for sometime after the end 🤔
[2023-12-08 23:32] .jferreira : but i didn't see a restart until now..
[2023-12-09 07:43] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Me too. Code for accepting a bid is quite easy (time is in seconds),  `if bidTime > endAuctionTime     can't accept new bid else if bidTime > endAuctionTime - 120     bidTime = bidTime + 60; end` when it stays for a while in "your bids" it has already a 'closed' auction status, that can't be moved back to 'open' state, at least from code.
[2023-12-09 10:01] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Mistery solved. It was because of the clock of the user device that wasn't aligned to real time, so the browser shown the auction as closed because the clock was running one minute ahead. This message is computed in the browser, so if the clock synchronization is not properly set it can give the feeling that the auction is closed while other users are still able to bid.

[2024-06-26 01:33] luchocogo : You can go with various strat.  Since the field is divided in 9 zones, and each player position affect different zones, each formation have his strong points and weakness.  For example, 4-4-2 is balanced in every aspect, but that means that increasing the quantity of players in defense will create advatange on your defensive zones, but ofc you will lose strenght on midfield and/or attack.  So if opp have a overall better team, increasing the strenght of your defensive zone may be the easiest solution.  But for example, if opp have a really offensive formation, you could try to reduce your midfield bonuses, and focus on a formation that have both a solid defense and attack. So your opp will have more chances against you, but with a better defensive bonuses, and on the other hand, you may have less attack situations, but at higher attack bonuses.

[2024-07-24 14:18] Deleted User : At this time, the current randomization is made, during draft: - Starting from potential, the final skills will be reached in 4 phases: Draft, pre-blooming, Blooming and post-blooming - A part (PBB) of this potential is assigned to the Pre-blooming and blooming phase (62% [std15%] of the total development), then split again to be part in the pre blooming (60% [std15%] of PBB) and the rest in the blooming phase. - The remaining part of the potential, once removed PBB, is assigned to the draft (60% [std10%]) and the rest to the post-blooming development. Note: 62% [std15%] means 62% in average, with a standard deviation of 15%. Players can be draft with age from 14 to 17.99 (very rare to have 14yo players, though), but this doesn't affect the development of the player at the end of the bloom.

[2024-10-07 05:00] ryanrumbles : <:keke:1037043588040757348>
[2024-10-07 07:01] .goosegod : Will not have impact on performance. Will only matter when you are on the attack and that player is involved in the build up. When he is involved his foot will be compared to the foot of the guy he goes against.  He gets a boost of 3% if the feet are the same on both players, or 6% if your guy is LR against either a L or an R. If the feet are opposite, the no bonus is given, or if both have LR again no bonus. It's in the guide under the Match section > Preferred foot.
[2024-10-07 07:06] .goosegod : Generally it's best to keep players on their preferred position. If they are on a different position, they lose some ability. It's displayed in the Lineup page when you hover over the players in field, under grade you will see some numbers, those will lower if you put them on another position, as indicated by a new number in brackets. Exception maybe be only of they have 8/I adaptability. In that case they may actually show a slightly bigger number on bracket on a different position. For example I have a 8/8 adaptability AMC that has higher score on FC position.

[2024-11-17 07:41] Deleted User : Is the period to recover lost GI same for both 1/8 and 8/8 adaptability players? And with how long they recover their lost GI?  The guide isn’t clear when it comes to that point

[2024-11-17 08:16] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Let me better explain what I mean with "recover". When a player loses some GI due to different factors (training structure level < 14, FP training, percentage training < 100%), means that a player will reach its max skills (its potential) later. Typically, the "extra GI" allows the player to reach its full potential earlier than 29yo (let's say 25yo-26yo). This extra GI can be quantified as something around 5% (statistically distributed) of the GI.

[2024-11-26 19:07] .jferreira : also, another question from other topic, if a player stop training position, it's because he can't train position nevermore or he may train on other week?
[2024-11-26 19:09] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Training position drains GI. If the player is old and GI is zero or negative, the GI cannot be drained and the position is not trained
[2024-11-26 19:12] .jferreira : but drain from that week alone?
[2024-11-26 19:13] .jferreira : or it drains from entire growth function?
[2024-11-26 19:31] Deleted User : What if i removed training position and now the player has 2 FP but different confidence levels. Does playing a player in his second FP to raise confidence drains GI as well?
[2024-11-26 19:40] selo1775 : If a player is removed from position training he will not gain confidence
[2024-11-26 22:07] led.lennon.atleticogranata : Each fp training (that occurs when the player plays) takes 1/3 of GI. Lets call the sum of this GI fractions taken as sumFpGI. The player accumulates these fraction of GI until the day of training. If your player has a positive GI, and the sumFpGI is > 1, then 1 GI is removed by the training and sumFpGI is reduced by 1. If sumFpGI > 6/3=2, 2 GIs are removed by the training and sumFpGI is reduced by 2. The maximum value of sumFpGI is 7/3. Once this maximum value is reached, fp training stops.

[2024-11-27 23:52] jcgotcandhustlecastle : What’s the best lineup out there? Or what works better? 4-4-2, 3-1-4-2, 3-5-2 or 3-2-3-2… any recommendations?

[2024-11-28 00:51] .jferreira : it's relative to your players's skills
[2024-11-28 17:26] luchocogo : All formations have pro and cons (Except the ones penalized by the ME).  The field is a 3x3 grid, where players add % coverage value depending on positions.  So, basically you have a total of 1000% coverage, distributed all over the field. If you remove a forward and add a defender, you are just trading attacking coverage for defensive coverage.  So to determine the best formation for a given match, you must choose where you want to invest more coverage compared to enemy team. And as Jofer says, you should also consider your players. Having more coverage on a zone means better bonuses on that zone to win clashes, but also means that the player selection to participate in that action is wider.

[2024-12-10 23:13] luchocogo : Advice on tactics are hard, since it's a little complex. I will reccomend you check how grid coverage works on the guide of the web, and then if you have questions, you can come here to ask specific ones.  With your cash, you can buy players, usually the reccomendation is to look for good 30+ cheap players, so you can make a base. Youngster are super expensive to buy at start.  Then you should increase stadium capacity. Just do little increase each time, until you notice your stadium isnt full.  Finally for improvements, you should always max the ones that give money. You have to choose your long term strategy, either build training and or academy facilities, or just work in the market. Other buildings are luxury you could afford later on.  QI is a coefficient that determine player quality, just like star reccomendation, but less visual xD

[2024-12-14 01:49] bene0321 : within the parentheses are the season ticket holders
[2024-12-14 02:13] bene0321 : when you're playing a match, you receive ticket income only from fans who do not own a season ticket. in example for covered seats, you received income only for 16 tickets (1500-1484=16).  the reason being, at the start of each season you can decide how many seats you want to allocate percentage wise to be open for sale of season tickets. the seats are bought for the whole season, so essentially you're getting a season's worth of ticket income already at the start of the season, based on your fanbase size and season ticket allocations. by default, your season ticket allocation is at 100% for all seat types, which theoretically means that all of your seats could be full of season ticket holders (you'll only receive ticket income if you build more seats after the season tickets have been sold).  the only "downside" is, that season tickets are sold at 80% (?) of the normal price.  I'm sure there is a more detailed description in the guides within the game, I recommend you check them out. I'm too tired rn to make any sense lmfao

[2024-12-19 01:22] Deleted User : I got a technical question
[2024-12-19 01:24] Deleted User : OMR + DMR would be as good as OMR + DR? (assuming the DMR and DR players are both 5 stars)
[2024-12-19 01:24] Deleted User : I guess OMR + DMR would be better as they would be closer to each other than using a DR?
[2024-12-19 03:35] .jferreira : not so simple OMR + DR will make OMR be selected to pivot more actions on FR and MR areas, DR will pivot more DR and DC, DMR will pivot more DR and MR
[2024-12-19 03:37] .jferreira : if you have a DMR with low pass/crossing and good heading, would be better to use him as DR and let OMR pivot the MR actions
[2024-12-19 03:38] .jferreira : if you have a DR with not heading, maybe would be better to use him as DMR for he don't pivot aerial defenses on DC area
[2024-12-19 03:40] .jferreira : if your offensive is on sides, could be good to have DMR to gain a little more coverage on MR and FR areas, but you could also just use a MR if your focus in on a specific side
[2024-12-19 11:34] luchocogo : Jofer already answered this perf, just a little last tip about what you writted, two players being close to another could help, since players not participating on a clash help with their energy on their coverage areas, but take in consideration that if you move your DR to DMR, for example, while it give more bonus on midfield and attack on their side, it reduce the bonus on the defensive zones.  So short answer is there isnt an optimal setup. Coverage is a short blanket, it depends on your strategy what you want to cover more or less.

[2025-02-17 06:41] led.lennon.atleticogranata : At this moment the ME is still a sequence of actions in which a player is selected as the pivot of the action on each side, clashes with the opponent comparing with the opponent by his skills (mainly) and skills of the players that have influence in that part of the pitch. Once won the clash, the action advances in the next zone of the pitch (zones are D, M, F, Box) and another pivot is selected. The "bug" is due to the fact that the ME doesn't check if the player selected as pivot is the same of the previous action, so it seems he is passing the ball to himself.  I hope soon will come a new version of the ME with the "passing" part of the action being better included into the flow.
[2025-02-17 06:44] led.lennon.atleticogranata : I think this is due to the strength of the two attacks compared with the weakness of the defense players. GK can be good, but if not supported by a good defense, it's like a pigeon shooting...

[2025-03-19 15:00] simsem : In the context of the game Trophy Manager, a good pre-bloom GI (General Improvement) typically refers to a player's performance or improvement before reaching the "bloom" phase, which is when a player's potential and attributes are fully realized. A good pre-bloom GI means the player is improving well in terms of stats, showing promise for higher performance when they fully bloom.  However, a good pre-bloom GI is not always a guarantee of success after blooming. A player might have a solid pre-bloom GI but then experience a poor bloom phase, meaning their growth and potential don't fully materialize, or they might develop weaknesses that hinder their future performance. Conversely

[2025-04-26 05:58] awesome_26632 : Hola, What's the benefits of Upgrading the u18 and u23 stadium 🏟️, does it have an impact in the players development?
[2025-04-26 07:19] wezbek_17184 : Do players get better by playing matches or is it only training that has an effect?
[2025-04-26 09:05] dustyklay : A bigger stadium for U18 and U23 teams brings more revenue for those teams, so you don't have to fund them too much by sending money from the main team. It has no impact on the player development.
[2025-04-26 09:07] dustyklay : The skills increase only through training, but matchs add routine, which helps with the player performances. Routine is kind of an additional skill layer.
[2025-04-26 09:09] wezbek_17184 : Alright thanks! Does U23/U18 matches count as official matches and give xp/routine?
[2025-04-26 09:11] dustyklay : Yes, they do. That's the main purpose of U23 and U18 teams, by the way, to add routine. A player who starts a game for the U23/U18 team gains more routine than a player who comes off the becnh for the main team.
